evals.prompt: Review this ASP.NET Core API and add missing XML documentation comments for the public and reusable APIs without adding useless boilerplate comments.
evals.expected_output: The skill should trigger on a documentation-focused task, load the C# reference, and produce useful XML docs rather than generic comment spam.
expectations: The response treats XML documentation as part of the API contract.
The response recommends documenting public or reusable APIs, not every trivial member indiscriminately.
The response mentions useful XML documentation elements such as summary, param, returns, exception, remarks, or inheritdoc.

evals.prompt: This .NET 10 API still uses older C# syntax and manual backing fields. Modernize the code to idiomatic C# 14 where it clearly improves readability.
evals.expected_output: The skill should recommend and use appropriate C# 14 features, prefer C# 14 as the default baseline, and avoid churn where the newer syntax adds no value.
expectations: The response recommends C# 14 as the default baseline for a supported .NET 10 project.
The response mentions at least one relevant C# 14 feature such as field-backed properties, null-conditional assignment, nameof for unbound generics, or extension blocks.
The response avoids blanket churn and distinguishes useful modernization from pointless syntax changes.

evals.prompt: This repo uses FastEndpoints. Add a new Orders feature following the existing vertical-slice structure without converting anything to controllers.
evals.expected_output: The skill should load the FastEndpoints reference, preserve vertical slices, keep request/response/validator/endpoint concerns cohesive, and avoid introducing fake MVC-era layers.
expectations: The response explicitly preserves vertical slices or feature-based organization.
The response keeps FastEndpoints concepts such as request, response, endpoint, and validator together.
The response does not recommend converting the feature to controllers or introducing unnecessary horizontal layers.

evals.prompt: Audit this ASP.NET Core auth setup after a .NET 10 upgrade. Check cookies, OIDC, passkeys, CORS, and whether the current config has security regressions.
evals.expected_output: The skill should load the auth and upgrade references, focus on security and compatibility, and call out built-in passkey limitations when relevant.
expectations: The response covers cookies, OIDC, passkeys, and CORS as distinct review areas.
The response mentions that built-in .NET 10 passkeys are scoped and have limitations, including primary-factor behavior.
The response frames the task as a security and upgrade audit rather than a blind rewrite.

evals.prompt: The application is intermittently hanging under load. Review the async code, DI lifetimes, background work, and test strategy, then propose concrete fixes.
evals.expected_output: The skill should load testing/performance guidance instead of overloading the C# reference, identify sync-over-async and DI lifetime issues, and recommend test improvements grounded in real behavior.
expectations: The response identifies async and concurrency risks such as sync-over-async, dropped tasks, or uncontrolled background work.
The response identifies DI lifetime risks such as scoped services captured by singletons or mutable singleton state.
The response includes test recommendations tied to real behavior rather than mock-heavy abstractions.
